summary.text: Kimberly Hardy is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent David Rouzer in North Carolina's 7th Congressional District.
A former school social worker with a Ph.D. in social work, she is a university social work professor and a vice chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party.
She previously ran for the North Carolina House in 2020 and 2022.

paragraphs.text: Hardy describes herself as raised by a police officer and a federal agent.
She earned a bachelor's degree from Morgan State University (1997), a master's in social work from Ohio State University, and a Ph.D. in social work from Morgan State University.
She worked as a school social worker before her academic career.

She has been an assistant professor of social work at the University of Connecticut (2010-2013) and the University of Saint Joseph (2013-2016), and later joined Fayetteville State University, where Port City Daily reports she is an associate professor.
Hardy was the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 43 (Fayetteville) in 2020, losing to Rep. Diane Wheatley (R) 51.8% to 48.2%, and she also campaigned for the seat in 2022.
She has served as second vice chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party.
She announced her 2026 candidacy for the 7th District in summer 2025; the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary was canceled and she advanced to the general election.

sources.title: Kimberly Hardy announces run against Rouzer for district 7 U.S. House seat
